memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: "Let my people go, so that they may worship me." If you refuse to let them go and continue to hold them back, the hand of the Lord will bring a terrible plague on your livestock in the field—on your horses, donkeys and camels and on your cattle, sheep and goats.'"" - Exodus 9:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once more the message goes out, and once more the same words: let my people go, so that they may worship me. God has not changed His request, and He has not softened it.

But notice the phrase continue to hold them back. God is naming an ongoing choice, not a single decision. Pharaoh is not being judged for one bad day; he is being judged for a persistent refusal that he renews every morning.

That distinction matters for us. Most of our spiritual danger lies not in one dramatic sin but in something we keep choosing — the grudge we continue to nurse, the honesty we continue to avoid, the obedience we continue to postpone.

And notice where the plague will fall. Livestock in Egypt were not merely property; several Egyptian deities were represented by cattle and rams. God is once again exposing the emptiness of what people worshipped.

He is patient. He is also serious. Both are true of the God we know in Jesus Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have I been "continuing" to hold back from God?
2. Which of my possessions or securities have quietly become objects of trust?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, show me where I am persistently resisting You. I let go of what I have been holding back. Amen.
